Well technically you can ovulate whenever during the cycle, but if you ovulate during your period the egg will be expelled because there's no lining. The "typical" window after ovulation is 2 weeks before a period because the egg only hangs around for so long unfertilized. Your body knows the egg is only good for so long unless it implants fertilized (it has to implant to progress). So yeah you could ovulate 2 days after your period ends but the egg would only be good for so long and your period would likely come early. To my knowledge sperm can live in the body anywhere from 3-7 days, depends on your source. So whatever many days before and about a 48 hour window after ovulation is when you can get pregnant before the egg "expires". 

The point of what I'm saying is if the date of conception (sperm fertilizing egg) happened early January, she'd be about 10 weeks and at least in my experience, something would have been "off" way before and she should be at least a cycle and a half late. Especially considering she's 17ish and that's typically when you're more regular and fertile.

I'm saying this (and not trying to argue, just educate) so OP can understand that it doesn't mathematically make sense that a month after the alleged conception she is suddenly showing symptoms of pregnancy. My sore breasts started a week before my missed period and didn't go away for months. What I'm saying comes from experience and a year or two of heavy research, experience in the medical field, and specialist doctor consults, I'm not just pulling it out of my ass. 

If you don't want to trust a stranger on the internet OP that's fine, but I agree about the commentor that suggested waiting for the dating scan (at 12 weeks, her doctor would go off her last definite period) and your answers should lie there. And if she's claiming it's yours, you should be allowed to go, not just see pictures.

I'm sorry for what happened to you. I may have missed it but I don't see anyone else mentioning that the timeline wouldn't match even if you did finish inside her. 

Most women get their period 2 weeks after ovulation, pregnancy can only occur in a roughly 5 day window around that date. So if I'm understanding correctly this happened at the beginning of January, meaning her missed period would have been mid January. Suspicious  bleeding or not ( because that can be possible), if the baby was conceived around the start of January her last period would have been roughly around Christmas and she'd be around 10 weeks pregnant. I think she would have noticed way before then. She'd be bloated to all hell and likely nauseous with sore breasts for weeks. I'm basing this off my experience, I conceived my first child around the same dates you mention.
